To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the buffering effect of social support and hardiness on the relationship between job stressors (i.e. job demand, role ambiguity and role conflict) and well-being was found in a limited number of cases only.
hardiness and support do not play a buffering or protective role, but they have a direct impact on well-being.
the buffering role of social support is confirmed, but only to a small degree, and that hardiness does not play a buffering or moderating role.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the buffering role of hardiness and social supports in relation to stressors.
the moderating role that hardiness and support play in the relation between job-related stressors and well-beings.
the role played by hardiness and social supports in the relation between job strain and the level of wellbeing of women working in offices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hardiness and the social support coming from supervisors do not play an important role in moderating the relation between job-related stressors and well- being.
hardiness and support are not strong buffers against stressors.
hardiness and the indexes of social support do not play a significant role in the relation between stressors and the level of well-beings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of social support in the buffering mechanism is limited.
the results are in accordance with the theory of the buffering role of social support and that the role of hardiness in this process is not significant.
hardiness and the indexes of social support do not constitute a protective factor in the case of office workers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary to consider the buffering role of hardiness and social supports when designing programs to prevent stress-related disorders in office workers.
hardiness and support do not have a strong buffering role in the case of women office workers.
social support is not a variable with a strong moderating role in the relation between job strain and well-being.
